mainTopic: Limits of the רבי מאיר / חכמים dispute about an unneeded אשם תלוי, and when property becomes ownerless after false testimony or a refused gift
overview: An אשם תלוי is a 'hanging' guilt offering that a person brings when he is unsure whether he sinned. If he later learns he never sinned, רבי מאיר says the animal becomes ordinary. The חכמים say it stays holy, because his worried heart (לבו נוקפו) made him dedicate it fully. The גמרא brings two limits to this argument. Even רבי מאיר agrees when the person set aside two animals as a backup. Even the חכמים agree when he set it aside only because of witnesses who were later proven זוממין. רבא challenges this second limit from the case of an ox sentenced to stoning, and אביי defends it. The same question turns out to be an argument between רבי אלעזר, who compares it to the מנחת קנאות, and רבי יוחנן, who says an offering brought for כפרה stays holy. The גמרא then discusses when property becomes ownerless so that anyone may take it: an ox whose witnesses were proven זוממין, a condemned city (עיר הנדחת), and a gift the receiver refuses. The question about the refused gift continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees when two animals were set aside as a backup
steps.stepSummary: This continues רבי אלעזר's statement that רבי מאיר agrees in one case. A person set aside two אשמות as a backup and got atonement with one of them. Then the second stays holy: it grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and its money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies when someone set aside two guilt offerings as a backup and got atonement with one of them. The second must graze until it gets a blemish, then be sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement that began just before this line: in this case even רבי מאיר agrees that the extra animal stays holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually רבי מאיר says a no-longer-needed אשם goes back to being ordinary. Here the leftover animal stays holy and is handled exactly the way the חכמים handle things. The case is special because the person picked two animals on purpose, so that one could replace the other.

keyTerms.meaning: As a guarantee or backup, in case one gets lost
He gained atonement (through the offering)
Becomes blemished and unfit for the altar
Gift offerings, here bought with the money for the communal altar

phrases.english: in a case where one sets aside two guilt offerings as a backup
and he gained atonement with one of them,
that the second one shall graze until it becomes blemished
and it shall be sold, and its money shall go to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַפְרִישׁ שְׁנֵי אֲשָׁמוֹת לְאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's statement from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two אשמות were set aside as a backup and one was used, even רבי מאיר holds the second stays holy and its money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר changes his usual view in the backup case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי מאיר agreeing. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר normally says the animal becomes ordinary. So we need to know what makes the two-animal case different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר agrees that the second backup animal stays holy.

steps.title: Setting aside two animals shows his conscience was bothering him
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees only when the person did not show that his heart was bothering him. Someone who set aside two animals, when one was enough, clearly showed that worry. So he fully meant to dedicate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר argues with the חכמים only because the person did not show that his conscience was bothering him. But here, he only needed to set aside one animal, so why did he set aside two? Because he thought: if one gets lost, I will get atonement with the other. Since he showed that his conscience was bothering him, he fully decided to make it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the two-animal case proves the person was truly worried about his sin. So even רבי מאיר agrees the dedication was complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument depends on לבו נוקפו, whether the person's conscience made him fully serious about the dedication. רבי מאיר does not reject that idea. He just says that with one animal, we can't see it. Picking an extra animal as a backup shows that worry openly, so the dedication holds even after it turns out he didn't sin.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue in this specific situation, not beyond it
He showed his thinking openly
His heart strikes him: his conscience bothers him
Gets lost
He fully decided and dedicated it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר agrees with the idea of לבו נוקפו. He only needs to see it openly, and setting aside two animals shows it.

phrases.english: They only disagree
Rabbi Meir with the Rabbis
because he did not show his thinking
that his heart was striking him,
but here, after all,
he only needed to set aside one;
why did he set aside two?
Because he thought: if one gets lost,
I will gain atonement with the other one.
And since he showed his thinking
that his heart was striking him,
since that was so,
he fully decided and dedicated it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר עֲלֵיהוֹן דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Setting aside a backup animal openly shows לבו נוקפו, so even רבי מאיר agrees the dedication was complete.

steps.title: The חכמים agree when the witnesses were proven false
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר in one case. If the אשם תלוי was brought because of witnesses who were later found to be עדים זוממין, the animal becomes ordinary and grazes with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about an אשם תלוי whose witnesses were proven to be עדים זוממין. The animal goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings the opposite kind of limit. In this case even the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that the animal is not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed a case where רבי מאיר moves toward the חכמים. This step shows a case where the חכמים move toward רבי מאיר. The case: witnesses said the person may have sinned, and they were later proven to be עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages agree (in this case)
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned
Were proven to be false plotting witnesses
It goes out and grazes with the flock: it is ordinary, not holy

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Meir
about a provisional guilt offering whose witnesses were proven false plotters,
that it goes out and grazes in the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel limit: this time the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי set aside because of witnesses who were later proven to be עדים זוממין becomes ordinary.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים give up their usual view in the case of false witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים usually say לבו נוקפו keeps the animal holy. So why not here?

keyTerms.meaning: Reason or logic behind a ruling

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים agree that the animal becomes ordinary when the witnesses were proven false.

steps.title: He never fully relied on the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say לבו נוקפו only when the person set the animal aside on his own. When he did it because of witnesses, he never fully relied on them. He knew other witnesses might come and prove them false, so he never fully dedicated it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים argue with him only when the person set it aside on his own, and then we say his conscience was bothering him. But when he set it aside because of witnesses, he did not rely on the witnesses. He thought: maybe others will come and prove them false.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the חכמים' reason, לבו נוקפו, only works when the person acted out of his own worry, not because witnesses told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness depends on how complete the person's decision was. Acting on his own conscience means he was fully serious. Acting only because of outside testimony means he always had a doubt in mind ('maybe they'll be proven false'). So his dedication was never complete, and once the witnesses are proven false, the animal is ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own, by his own choice
Because of witnesses' testimony
Relies on
Prove them to be עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין (false plotting witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: Both limits come from the same idea: the animal stays holy only if the person truly and fully meant to dedicate it (לבו נוקפו). A backup animal shows full intent. Relying on witnesses shows the intent was never complete.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the חכמים give up the idea of לבו נוקפו. They hold it as before. It just does not apply when the person never fully relied on the witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: The Rabbis only disagree with him

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּאַפְרְשֵׁיהּ עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: where he set it aside on his own,
and we say his heart was striking him;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּעַל פִּי עֵדִים אַפְרְשֵׁיהּ –
phrases.english: but where he set it aside because of witnesses,
he was not relying on the witnesses,
for he thought: maybe others will come
and prove them to be false plotting witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When he set it aside because of witnesses, he never fully relied on them, so לבו נוקפו does not apply and the dedication was never complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 3, this shows that the whole argument is about how complete the person's intent was when he dedicated the animal.

steps.title: רבא quotes the case of the ox sentenced to stoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a challenge by quoting the משנה: an ox sentenced to stoning is different, because if the case falls apart before the stoning, the ox goes out and grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: An ox that is to be stoned is not like this. If [the testimony falls apart] before it was stoned, it goes out and grazes in the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a challenge against רב by quoting a line from the משנה about a שור הנסקל. He is setting up his argument; the actual attack comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts the ox with the אשם תלוי. If the case against the ox falls apart before the stoning, the ox simply goes back to being a normal animal. רבא will now ask exactly what kind of 'falling apart' the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox sentenced to be stoned (for killing a person)
It goes out and grazes in the flock, meaning it is just an ordinary animal again

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
An ox that is to be stoned is not like this,
phrases.notes: 'Not like this' means not like the אשם תלוי case that the משנה was just discussing.

phrases.english: if [the case falls apart] before it was stoned –
it goes out and grazes in the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב's statement in step 4 by quoting the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement (step 4) that the חכמים agree when the אשם תלוי was set aside because of witnesses who turned out to be עדים זוממין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ox line will be used to show what kind of case the משנה has in mind.

steps.title: What kind of case is the ox case?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the ox case looks like. It can't be two witnesses against two witnesses, because then there is no reason to believe the second pair over the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say two witnesses came and said 'it killed,' and two others said 'it did not kill,' why do you listen to the later pair? Listen to the first pair!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is working out what kind of case the ox line describes. He rules out one possibility, two witnesses against two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two witnesses contradict two other witnesses, neither pair wins. The second pair has no more weight than the first. So that kind of contradiction could never free the ox, and the משנה must mean something stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? How does the case look?
A pair of witnesses, two people
What did you see? Why prefer one side over the other?
Listen to, believe

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that two came and said 'it killed,'
and two [others] say 'it did not kill' –
what did you see that you listen to the later ones?
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, so read it as 'you listen.'

phrases.english: Listen to the first ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the ox case from step 7 and rules out the two-against-two reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of event makes the case against the ox fall apart?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not two witnesses against two, since the second pair has no extra weight.

steps.title: So the משנה is about false witnesses, and the חכמים still argue
steps.stepSummary: The ox case must be about עדי הזמה. The matching אשם תלוי case is then also about עדי הזמה, and there the חכמים disagree. That goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about עדי הזמה? And the matching case of the אשם תלוי is also about עדי הזמה, and yet they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge. If the ox case is about עדי הזמה, the אשם תלוי case right next to it must be too, and the חכמים argue there. That contradicts רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדי הזמה are believed over the first pair, so that is the only way the ox case can work. The משנה sets the ox case and the אשם תלוי case side by side, so both should be about the same kind of situation. In the אשם תלוי case the חכמים do not say it grazes, yet רב said they agree it grazes when witnesses are proven false.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? (introduces the only reading left)
Witnesses proven false because others testify they were elsewhere at the time
And the matching case, the parallel to it
They disagree

steps.whyThisMatters: If רבא is right, רב's rule (step 4) cannot stand, because the משנה itself would show the חכמים disagreeing in the false-witness case.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it with עדי הזמה?
phrases.notes: These are the second pair saying 'you were with us somewhere else then.' That kind of testimony is believed over the first pair.

phrases.english: And the matching case regarding the אשם תלוי –
is with עדי הזמה, and they disagree!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר and do not let the animal go back to the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּעֵדֵי הֲזָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the case analysis in step 8 and turns it against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim (step 4) that the חכמים agree in a case of עדים זוממין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ox case can only be about עדי הזמה. The parallel אשם תלוי case is then also about עדי הזמה, and there the חכמים disagree, which is the opposite of what רב said.

steps.title: אביי: maybe the 'killed' man walked in alive
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ox case may not be about witnesses at all. It could be that the supposedly killed person came walking into court.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe the ox case is where the 'killed' person came on his own feet.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רבא's proof. He offers a different picture of the ox case that has nothing to do with false witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thought the only way to clear the ox was through עדי הזמה. אביי points out a clearer way: the 'victim' shows up alive, so everyone sees the testimony was wrong. Once the ox case is not about witnesses, the matching אשם תלוי case does not have to be about witnesses either.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (opens a different way to read the source)
The 'killed' person coming on his own feet, clear proof that no one was killed

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבא's case is impossible. He is only saying the משנה doesn't have to be about עדי הזמה, so it can't serve as a proof.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But perhaps, what is the case of the ox to be stoned –
for example, where the 'killed' person came on his own feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's claim in steps 8–9 that the ox case must be about עדי הזמה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. אביי rejects רבא's reading of the ox case, not the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא missed a third possibility: the victim appears alive. That clears the ox without any witnesses.

steps.title: The matching אשם תלוי case: the fat turned out to be permitted
steps.stepSummary: The parallel אשם תלוי case is where it became known that the piece he ate was permitted. When he set the animal aside because of witnesses, the חכמים agree it grazes, just as רב said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the matching case of the אשם תלוי is where it became known what the piece was. But where he set aside the אשם תלוי because of witnesses, no [the חכמים do not argue].
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer. In the משנה, the אשם תלוי case is one where the facts became clear on their own, not through witnesses, so רב's rule about witnesses still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox case and the אשם תלוי case match because both are cleared by plain facts, not by witnesses. The חכמים argue only in that kind of case. When the man set aside the animal because of witnesses, he never fully meant to dedicate it (step 6), so even the חכמים agree it goes out and grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: The piece became known, meaning it became clear what the doubtful piece of fat really was
He set it aside, designated it
Because of the testimony of witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case where the חכמים argue is one where the facts cleared him on their own, like the fat proving permitted. When he set the animal aside because of witnesses who were later proven false, the חכמים agree it grazes. So רב's rule stands.

phrases.english: And the matching case regarding the אשם תלוי –
for example, where the piece became known.
phrases.notes: It became clear that the doubtful piece he ate was permitted fat, so he never sinned.

phrases.english: But where he set it aside as an אשם תלוי
because of witnesses – no.
phrases.notes: 'No' means the חכמים do not argue there. They agree it goes out and grazes, just as רב said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִכְווֹתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי אָשָׁם תָּלוּי – כְּגוֹן דְּהוּכְּרָה חֲתִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 10 by applying it to the parallel אשם תלוי case, which saves רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the משנה's אשם תלוי dispute is about facts becoming clear, not about witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא assumed the משנה's אשם תלוי case involved עדי הזמה, so the חכמים disagree even with false witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's dispute is about a case like the fat proving permitted. With witnesses, the חכמים agree it grazes, as רב taught.

steps.title: The case of witnesses proven זוממין is a known dispute: רבי אלעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that an אשם תלוי whose witnesses were proven זוממין is a dispute. רבי אלעזר compares it to a מנחת קנאות, which goes out to חולין when the witnesses are proven זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a matter of dispute. If a person set aside an אשם תלוי because of witnesses, and those witnesses were proven זוממין: רבי אלעזר says it is like a מנחת קנאות. As a ברייתא teaches: if the witnesses against her were found to be זוממין, her מנחה goes out to חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the argument over an אשם תלוי whose witnesses turned out to be זוממין, between רב (quoted by רב יהודה) and רבא, matches an existing argument between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן. It first brings רבי אלעזר's opinion, which fits רב's view that the animal becomes ordinary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר learns from the מנחת קנאות of a סוטה. If the witnesses who started her process are proven זוממין, her מנחה simply loses its holiness. In the same way, the אשם תלוי was set aside only because of the false witnesses, so it goes back to being ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a matter of dispute
A provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
His witnesses were proven זוממין, meaning they were shown to have been somewhere else
The 'meal offering of jealousy' brought in the סוטה process
It goes out to ordinary, non-holy status

phrases.english: It is a matter of dispute:
A provisional guilt offering whose witnesses were proven conspiring –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: it is like a meal offering of jealousy,
as it is taught: if her witnesses were found to be conspiring –
phrases.notes: 'Her' means the סוטה, the woman whose process brings the מנחת קנאות.

phrases.english: her meal offering goes out to non-sacred status.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי שֶׁהוּזַּמּוּ עֵדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the רב / רבא argument (steps 4–11) matches the dispute between רבי אלעזר (like רב) and רבי יוחנן (like רבא).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, an אשם תלוי whose witnesses were proven זוממין loses its holiness, just like a מנחת קנאות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the animal stays holy and grazes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the animal grazes until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and the money goes to נדבה offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold, and its money goes to the fund for נדבה offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the dispute. רבי יוחנן says the animal does not go back to being ordinary, which fits רבא's view that the חכמים disagree even when the witnesses are proven false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the holiness stays on the animal even though the witnesses were proven liars. Because it cannot be brought as an אשם, it waits for a blemish and is redeemed. Its money is used for communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes until it becomes blemished
It is sold, which redeems it
Voluntary gift offerings

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: it shall graze until it becomes blemished
and it shall be sold, and its money shall go to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, an אשם תלוי whose witnesses were proven זוממין stays holy. It grazes, is redeemed once blemished, and its money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוחנן compare it to מנחת קנאות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: he should compare the אשם תלוי to the מנחת קנאות, which goes to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, let him compare it to the מנחת קנאות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. It asks why he does not accept רבי אלעזר's comparison, which seems so natural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve something made holy because of witnesses who turned out to be זוממין. The ברייתא says the מנחה goes to חולין. So why should the אשם תלוי stay holy?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him compare it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan, let him compare it to a meal offering of jealousy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, נְדַמְּיֵיהּ לְמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling using רבי אלעזר's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the אשם תלוי stays holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about מנחת קנאות shows that something made holy because of witnesses later proven זוממין goes back to חולין. The same should apply here.

steps.title: The cases differ: an אשם תלוי comes for כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת קנאות only comes to clear up whether she sinned. An אשם תלוי comes for כפרה, so the owner's worried heart makes him set it aside completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not alike. The מנחת קנאות does not come for כפרה; it only comes to clear up whether there was a sin. But an אשם תלוי comes for כפרה. Since his heart bothers him, he makes up his mind fully and makes it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. It shows why the two cases are not truly alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the witnesses are proven false, the מנחת קנאות has no job left, since its only purpose was to clarify her sin. A person bringing an אשם תלוי wants כפרה, so when he dedicated it he was worried that he may have sinned. So he sets the animal aside with full intent, and that holiness does not depend on the witnesses being right.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
To clear up whether there was a sin
His heart bothers him; he feels guilty
He fully decides and makes it holy

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's point: an offering brought for כפרה is set aside with a full heart, so it stays holy even if the witnesses turn out false. The מנחת קנאות, which only clarifies the facts, goes back to חולין.

phrases.english: It is not similar:
a meal offering of jealousy does not come for atonement,
but rather to clarify a sin.
But a provisional guilt offering, which comes for atonement,
since his heart strikes him, he resolves fully and consecrates it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דָּמֵי, מִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת לָא לְכַפָּרָה קָאָתְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases seem alike, since both were made holy because of witnesses later proven זוממין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת קנאות only exists to clarify the facts. The אשם תלוי comes for כפרה, so the owner set it aside with full intent, and it stays holy.

steps.title: A שור הנסקל whose witnesses were proven זוממין is ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רבי כרוספדאי quotes רבי יוחנן: if a שור הנסקל's witnesses are proven זוממין, anyone who grabs the ox acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי כרוספדאי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: an ox sentenced to stoning whose witnesses were proven זוממין belongs to whoever takes hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about the ox case from earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner heard that his ox would be stoned, he gave up ownership, since a stoned ox is useless to him. So even after the witnesses are proven liars, the ox stays ownerless, and the first person to take it gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox sentenced to stoning
Whoever takes hold of it acquires it
Ownerless property

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Keruspedai said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
an ox that is to be stoned whose witnesses were proven conspiring –
anyone who takes possession of it acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל שֶׁהוּזַּמּוּ עֵדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אשם תלוי to a related rule about the שור הנסקל whose witnesses were proven זוממין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שור הנסקל whose witnesses were proven זוממין is ownerless, and whoever takes hold of it acquires it.

steps.title: רבא limits רבי יוחנן's rule to when the ox was the victim
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוחנן's rule makes sense only when the witnesses said someone else did the act with the ox. If they accused the owner himself, he knows it is false, so he does not give up the ox. Instead he works to bring other witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן's reason makes sense when the witnesses told him, 'Your ox was used for bestiality.' But if they said, 'He did bestiality with his ox,' he himself knows that he did not do it. So he does not give it up; instead, he makes the effort and brings witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the reason behind רבי יוחנן's rule. He uses that reason to limit the rule to one kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner only gives up his ox if he believes the witnesses. When they say someone else did the act, he has no way to know they are lying. When they accuse the owner himself, he knows the truth, so he holds on to the ox and tries to prove them זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense
Was the victim of bestiality (done by someone else)
He committed bestiality
Gives up ownership; makes it ownerless
He makes an effort

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נִרְבַּע and רָבַע. נִרְבַּע means the ox was the victim and someone else did it. רָבַע means the owner himself did it, and only in that case does he know the witnesses are lying.
steps.whatToRemember: Giving up ownership depends on what the owner believes. If he knows the witnesses are lying, he never gives up his ox, so it is not ownerless.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rava said: the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan makes sense
where they said to him: his ox was used for bestiality.
But if they said: he committed bestiality with his ox,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ מִידָּע יָדַיע דְּלָא רְבַע
phrases.english: he himself surely knows that he did not commit it
and he does not give up ownership of it,
but he makes an effort and brings witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's rule from the previous step, based on the reason behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ox is ownerless only when the witnesses accused someone else of the act. If they accused the owner himself, he knows they lied, so he keeps ownership.

steps.title: Why is the condemned city different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from ריש לקיש's ruling that when the witnesses against an עיר הנדחת are made זוממין, anyone who grabs the city's property acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and what רבה בר איתי said in the name of ריש לקיש: if the witnesses against an עיר הנדחת are made זוממין, anyone who takes hold of its property acquires it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's idea that a person who knows the accusation is false does not give up his property. It points to the עיר הנדחת, where the property does become free for anyone to take.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an עיר הנדחת, the people also know they did not worship idols, just like the owner in step 17 knows he did not sin with his ox. Yet ריש לקיש says they gave up their property. So why should the ox owner be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? (a way of asking why two cases are treated differently)
A city whose people were led to worship idols. Its property must be burned.
Its witnesses were proven to be עדים זוממין (false witnesses)
The one who takes hold of it (takes possession)
Acquired it, became its owner

phrases.english: And what is different from that

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אִיתַּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: which Rabba bar Ittai said that Reish Lakish said:
An idolatrous city whose witnesses were proven false (zomemim)
anyone who takes hold of it acquires it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the city's property. The people knew they were innocent, and still it counts as given up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אִיתַּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reasoning in step 17 by using a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that an owner who knows he is innocent does not give up his property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In an עיר הנדחת the residents also know they are innocent, yet their property counts as given up after the witnesses are made זוממין.

steps.title: Many people versus one person
steps.stepSummary: In an עיר הנדחת, each person thinks others sinned and the city will be burned anyway, so he gives up his property. With the ox, everything depends on the owner, so he fights the false testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עיר הנדחת involves many people. Each one thinks: I did not sin, but someone else did, and he gives up his property. Here, the matter depends on the owner alone. He knows he did not sin with the animal, so he does not give it up. He works to bring other witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows why the city and the ox are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether an עיר הנדחת is condemned depends on what the many residents did, so one innocent person cannot be sure of the result and gives up hope. The ox owner's case depends only on himself. Because he knows the witnesses are lying, he expects to win and never gives up the ox.

keyTerms.meaning: Many people
Gives up ownership, makes it הפקר (ownerless)
Had relations with an animal (the sin that makes an ox a שור הנסקל)
Makes an effort

steps.whatToRemember: Property becomes ownerless only if the owner really gave up on it. Many people sharing one fate makes each one give up. One person who knows he is innocent keeps fighting.

phrases.english: An idolatrous city, which involves many people,
each one says to himself:
I did not sin, but someone else sinned,
and so he gives up ownership of his property.
But here, where the matter depends on him alone,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ox from step 17, where the witnesses accused the owner himself.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ מִידָּע יָדַע דְּלָא רְבַע,
phrases.english: he himself surely knows that he did not sin with the animal,
and he does not give it up,
but rather he makes the effort and brings witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, דְּרַבִּים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by showing a real difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (many people versus one person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The residents of an עיר הנדחת are like the ox owner, so the owner should give up his property too.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a city, each person thinks others sinned and gives up hope. The ox owner's case depends only on himself, so he keeps the ox and fights the testimony.

steps.title: A gift the receiver refuses
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that if someone is given a gift and says "I do not want it," anyone who takes it acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: If someone gives a gift to his friend, and the friend says "I do not want it," anyone who takes hold of it acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of ריש לקיש about another case where anyone who grabs an item acquires it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying "I do not want it," the receiver gives up the gift. It does not go back to the giver. Instead it becomes ownerless, so anyone may take it.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
I do not want it
That other person (here, the receiver)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
One who gives a gift to his friend,
and that one said: "I do not want it" –
anyone who takes hold of it acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הַנּוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case built on the same idea: anyone who grabs an item acquires it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift the receiver refuses with "I do not want it" becomes ownerless, and anyone who takes it acquires it.

steps.title: Challenge from רב ששת on canceling a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש's ruling fits with רב ששת's ruling. רב ששת says a receiver who says "I do not want it" after the gift reached his hand cancels the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and what רבה בר אבוה said in the name of רב ששת (some say רבי אבהו said it in the name of רב ששת)? A receiver who, after the gift came into his hand, said "Let this gift be void," "It is voided," or "I do not want it" — his words stand. If he said "It is void" or "It is not a gift" — he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with another ruling about the same words, "I do not want it." The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת says "I do not want it" cancels the gift, so the gift is undone, not left ownerless for anyone to grab. That seems to clash with ריש לקיש, who says anyone may take it. רב ששת also lists certain wordings, like "It is void" and "It is not a gift," that do not work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who receives a gift
Let it be void (from now on)
It is (hereby) voided
It is void (as if it was never a real gift)
His words stand (they take effect)
He said nothing (his words have no effect)

phrases.english: And what is different from that

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: which Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav Sheshet said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Abbahu said that Rav Sheshet said:
A receiver of a gift who said
after the gift came into his hand:
"Let this gift be void," "It is voided,"
"I do not want it" – his words stand.
"It is void," "It is not a gift" –
he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling in step 20 with another ruling about the same words.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that a refused gift is free for anyone to grab
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת says "I do not want it" cancels the gift, which suggests it goes back rather than becoming ownerless for anyone to take.
